summary.headline: City Union Bank Q1 FY27 PAT rose 25% YoY to Rs 383 crore, a record, with GNPA down to 1.73% and NIM guided to 3.65-3.70%.
summary.overview: Advances grew 25% YoY to Rs 67,645 crore and deposits 21% to Rs 79,342 crore, with CD ratio at 85%. Operating profit rose 29% to Rs 581 crore and PAT 25% to Rs 383 crore, both stated as record highs. Asset quality improved further: GNPA 1.73% (from 2.99% a year ago), Net NPA 0.61%, and recoveries exceeded slippages. Management guided to a moderate NIM dip from higher cost of funds, cost-to-income of 47-48% for FY27, and an exit ROA of 1.60-1.65%.

financial_highlights.change: up 25% QoQ as stated; vs Rs 54,020 crore in 1QFY26

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: MSME average disbursement about Rs 3,500 crore per quarter; management targets MSME at 55-60% of book and growth 2-3% above system. Average utilisation fell from 73% to 70%; repayments about Rs 900 crore per month.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Share of book at 30-31%, guided to stay 31-32%. Agri gold yield about 10-10.5% and non-agri 11-11.5%; agri priced 100 bps lower. Average LTV 62.07%. Branches rose from 700 to 1,000.

segments.name: Retail secured (LAP)
segments.commentary: LAP yield about 9.60-9.70%. Management expects retail secured at about 10% of book.

segments.name: Investments
segments.commentary: Yield on investments fell to 6.42% from 6.61% in 4QFY26 because Rs 12 crore of mutual fund income (on about Rs 700 crore invested) was classified under other income; 6.67% on an interest-income basis.

guidance_outlook: Advances growth guided at 2-3% above industry credit growth for FY27; DSA business about 1-2% of book.
NIM expected at 3.65-3.70% over the next few quarters as cost of deposits rises about 5 bps; long-term view 3.70-3.75%.
Cost of deposits guided at 5.60-5.70%; borrowing cost of about Rs 94 crore per quarter for the next two quarters.
Cost-to-income guided at 47-48% for FY27 (currently 45%) because staff hikes start from July; long-term aspiration below 45% in about three years.
Exit ROA guided at 1.60-1.65%; full-year ROA 1.55-1.65%. Steady-state credit cost about 0.40%; FY27 slippages Rs 700-750 crore; slippage ratio 1.20-1.30%.
ECLGS participation: Rs 800 crore disbursed to date; total expected Rs 2,000-2,500 crore. ECL provisioning about 0.45% of loan book, CAR consumption capped at 0.65%.
capex_capacity: Branch rollout front-loaded this year; branch count rose from 700 to 1,000 in the gold-loan context.
AI-led automation invested in operations; management expects it to lower cost further.

Business enterprise (non-MSME, no Udyam registration) loans at Rs 18,827 million; large-industry book fell from Rs 22,500 million (Dec-25) to about Rs 15,000 million then rose to Rs 19,000 million on exits and yield pressure.
demand_pricing: Gold loan rates unchanged; management ruled out raising rates to slow growth, citing agri customer needs and competitiveness in non-agri gold; rates up 20-25 bps over last year.
MSME utilisation fell to 70% from 73-74% norm; management attributes it to cautious borrowers and sees it recovering with textile demand after the European trade agreement.
Term deposit rates expected to rise on high demand; FCNR window brought in fresh deposits of Rs 150 crore.
SMA-0/1/2 at 1.20%/0.70%/0.90% (total 2.85%), down from 7.12% in June 2025 and 10.78% in September 2024. Domestic consumption said to be insulated from West Asia stress.
Fee income fell about 15% YoY and 19% in one comparison per analyst question; management expects catch-up in Q2-Q4 from processing fees, suit recoveries and insurance.

qa_highlights.question: How will margins move beyond the near-term cost-of-funds increase (FY27-FY28 levers), given stagnant lending yields?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to MSME, gold and retail secured yields (agri gold ~10-10.5%, non-agri 11-11.5%, LAP 9.60-9.70%, MSME 9.30-9.40%) and a low-cost deposit franchise; long-term NIM view 3.70-3.75%. The Q1 cost-of-funds decline was attributed to better repricing and lower borrowing cost.

qa_highlights.question: Why is MSME growing about 15% when system MSME growth is above 20%? Is utilisation falling?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited Rs 900 crore monthly repayments, MSME utilisation down to 70% from a 73-74% norm, and slightly more cautious pricing. Guidance is MSME growth 2-3% above system, with MSME at 55-60% of book.

qa_highlights.question: What slippage and credit cost levels are sustainable over one to two years?
qa_highlights.answer: Steady-state credit cost about 0.40%; FY27 slippages Rs 700-750 crore; slippage ratio 1.20-1.30%. Recoveries have exceeded slippages for about 10 quarters and are expected to continue.

qa_highlights.question: How will the bank reach 25-30% higher growth with the mix intact (gold 31-32%, MSME 55-60%, retail 10%), and what is the MSME outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated the mix targets and said lower utilisation cost about 3-4% of MSME growth. It expects MSME growth 2-3% above system, with the European trade agreement seen supporting textile utilisation.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the rise in cost of funds despite lower deposit costs, and what is the treasury and borrowing cost outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Borrowing cost rose to Rs 94 crore from Rs 72.5 crore in 4QFY26; treasury gains were Rs 52.54 crore vs Rs 29 crore in 4QFY26. Borrowing cost is guided at about Rs 94 crore per quarter for the next two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: How is the bank participating in ECLGS, and how is the ECL provisioning assessed?
qa_highlights.answer: Rs 800 crore disbursed to date (Rs 200 crore last quarter); total expected Rs 2,000-2,500 crore. ECL provision about 0.45% of loan book, with CAR consumption capped at 0.65%; flow impact described as negligible given the secured book.

qa_highlights.question: Why did fee income decline and how will it recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Fee income was down about 15% YoY (analyst cited 19% in one comparison). Management expects catch-up in Q2-Q4 from processing fees, suit recoveries and insurance income; non-treasury other income was Rs 243 crore in Q1 vs roughly Rs 300 crore in Q4 last year.

risks_watch: Utilisation trend in MSME (70% in Q1 vs 73-74% norm) and whether the European trade-agreement recovery in textiles materialises.
Cost of deposits moving to 5.60-5.70% and the ~5 bps NIM hit; NIM guided 3.65-3.70%, below the 3.78% reported in Q1.
Cost-to-income rising to 47-48% for FY27 from 45.42% as staff hikes start from July; exit ROA 1.60-1.65% depends on fee income recovery.
Gold loan pricing: management ruled out rate hikes, so growth is supported only by volume; agri gold LTV around 62% with sensitivity to gold price drops.
West Asia stress and SMA trends (SMA-0/1/2 total 2.85%) and ECLGS-linked disbursements that may affect future asset quality.
Large-industry book volatility (Rs 22,500 million in Dec-25, down to ~Rs 15,000 million, then ~Rs 19,000 million) and the non-MSME business enterprise book of Rs 18,827 million.
key_quotes: For 1QFY27 as well, we have achieved 25% credit growth quarter-on-quarter, the highest growth rate in June-to-June and our advances had increased to Rs. 67,645 crores from Rs. 54,020 crores in 1QFY26.
So, the trend of recovery more than slippages continues, and we are confident of maintaining recovery more than slippages for the next quarter as well, which is the current quarter.
So, we are quite confident of maintaining the cost-to-income at 47%. We are currently at 45 as we speak.
We haven't changed any rate of interest for gold loans. We are at the same rate, and we continue to do the same.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident and specific on asset quality, recoveries and growth targets, repeating FY27 guidance from the Q4 call. It was cautious on margins, cost-to-income and fee income, and deflected on the MSME utilisation decline and gold pricing rather than offering new numbers.

adds.what: Gold loan branches rose from 700 to 1,000; branch rollout front-loaded this year

growth.why: Management guides advances 2-3% above industry credit growth for FY27 and FY27 ROA of 1.55-1.65%, backed by gold-loan branch expansion (700 to 1,000), a stated share of gold book at 31-32%, and MSME demand recovery expectations; no specific new capacity or order book quantified for growth beyond these.
